additions.name: Telehouse Frankfurt Building N — new 3.6 MW IT data centre

status.summary: Telehouse's press release of 1 September 2026 announces the official opening of its new data centre, Building N, on its Frankfurt campus, says it was put into service this summer after progressive commissioning in the first half of 2026, and says it was fully let before it opened. Building N is therefore operating as of 1 September 2026. The status covers Building N only: the campus's other data-centre buildings are not assessed here, the further data centre Telehouse is planning on the campus is not part of it, and the 3.6 MW IT and 4.5 MW electrical figures are design capacities, not measured load or utilisation.

locator.precision: Official City of Frankfurt building-address point for Kleyerstraße 75-87 (address object DEHEFALK4mb00001), the address Telehouse publishes for its Frankfurt campus and its new data centre. It locates the campus at its registered street address, not Building N's footprint, a parcel or the campus boundary.
locator.identity_review: Telehouse's 1 September 2026 release places Building N on its Frankfurt campus. Telehouse Deutschland's page for the new data centre gives the same figures (about 2,200 m2 of colocation space, 3.6 MW, 4.5 MW total), says it extends Telehouse's own campus and gives the address Kleyerstrasse 75-87, 60326 Frankfurt; its locations page places the Frankfurt campus in the Kleyerstraße, and the December 2023 Building M release describes the same campus and its heat supply to the neighbouring FRANKY quarter, which Mainova's 16 October 2026 article also attributes to the neighbouring Telehouse data centre. The geoportal returns exactly one building-address feature for 'Kleyerstraße 75-87', and each single number from 75 to 87 resolves to that same object, so the range is one registered address. The service's configuration declares EPSG:25832, and the point was transformed with pyproj 3.7.1 (round trip 2 mm). Neither the city centre nor a head-office address is used: the campus address is also Telehouse Deutschland's own, but here it is the published address of the data-centre campus. The 16 October 2026 hold's reference to a former Databurg campus came from trade reporting; Telehouse's own pages place the new building at Kleyerstraße 75-87.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The address register publishes no positional accuracy. The point is a single address point at the campus street frontage, and Telehouse does not publish where Building N stands on the roughly 67,000 m2 campus.

additions.site_name: VIRTUS Saunderton Data Centre Campus (Haw Lane, Saunderton, Buckinghamshire)
additions.name: VIRTUS Saunderton Campus - LONDON15 to LONDON18 (four data centres, 78 MW IT planned)

status.summary: VIRTUS Data Centres' press release dated 24 September 2026 says its new £2.45 billion financing package supports the next phase of expansion, which includes 'the development of the company's 78 MW, AI-ready Saunderton campus in Buckinghamshire'. This dated company disclosure names the Saunderton campus as a development VIRTUS is funding, supporting announced status as of 24 September 2026. The campus is the four-building Saunderton Data Centre Campus (London 15 to London 18) at Haw Lane, Saunderton, for which Virtus Holdco Ltd applied to the Environment Agency for a bespoke permit (EPR/SP3429LN/A001; consultation 28 July to 25 August 2026). No consent, site works or construction stage is asserted: VIRTUS's 2024 statements that the site had approved planning and would be built from Q4 2024 for service in Q2 2026 are old and forecast, and no in-window record of planning consent or physical work was found.

locator.precision: Site grid reference (Ordnance Survey National Grid 480790 198500) given in Virtus Holdco Ltd's non-technical summary for environmental-permit application EPR/SP3429LN/A001, published by the Environment Agency, converted to WGS84 with pyproj 3.7.1 (EPSG:27700 to EPSG:4326). It is a reference point for the whole four-building Saunderton campus; it is not a building footprint, the installation boundary or a surveyed position.
locator.identity_review: The non-technical summary names the Saunderton Data Centre Campus of four new data-centre buildings, London 15 to London 18, at Haw Lane, Saunderton, Buckinghamshire HP14 4JD, and the Environment Agency's consultation page lists the same applicant (Virtus Holdco Limited), site and address. VIRTUS's location page describes its Saunderton Campus as four data centres with 78 MW of IT load on more than 50 acres, the same 78 MW Saunderton campus named in its 24 September 2026 release; its February 2024 release places the campus on a 50-acre freehold plot in Saunderton. The NTS site-location figure outlines the site south of Haw Lane and west of the railway near Saunderton station. In Esri World Imagery viewed locally (not redistributed), the point falls near the middle of a large cleared and graded compound in that position. The ONS centroid of HP14 4JD lies about 183 m north at the Haw Lane frontage and is not used. No geocoder, city-centre point or estate centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The non-technical summary gives the grid reference in whole tens of metres with no stated accuracy and does not say which part of the site it marks; the campus covers more than 50 acres, so its buildings extend a few hundred metres around the point.

additions.site_name: Graven Hill D1 Site (Circular Road, Ambrosden, Bicester, Oxfordshire)
additions.name: Graven Hill D1 Data Centre Campus - eight data-centre units (Cherwell reserved matters 25/03310/REM)

status.summary: On 6 August 2026 Cherwell District Council approved reserved matters application 25/03310/REM (appearance, landscaping, layout and scale) pursuant to outline planning permission 22/01829/OUT (granted 10 October 2023) for the redevelopment of the Graven Hill D1 Site at Ambrosden, near Bicester. The council's officer report describes the approved scheme as eight data-centre units totalling 103,605 sq m GIA within the approved B8 use: Unit 1 a 15 MW building of 4,288 sq m and Units 2-8 60 MW buildings of 13,961 sq m each, with diesel standby generators and an on-site substation. With the outline permission, this issued approval is the planning consent for the data-centre development, so permitted status is supported as of 6 August 2026. No construction is established: the former depot buildings were demolished earlier under a separate permission, and the applicant has since (18 September 2026) lodged an alternative reserved matters application for ten warehouse buildings on the same site, which is undecided and does not revoke the data-centre approval.
status.permit_reference: Cherwell District Council approval of reserved matters 25/03310/REM (decision 2026-08-06) pursuant to outline planning permission 22/01829/OUT (granted 2023-10-10)
status.permit_identity_review: The decision notice approves the reserved matters for application 25/03310/REM at Unit D1 Graven Hill, Circular Road, Ambrosden, and binds the development to plans that include the 'Graven Hill D1 Site - Data Centre' area schedule and typical 60 MW and 15 MW unit drawings. The delegated officer report for the same reference states that the application seeks permission for 8 data-centre units totalling 103,605 sq m GIA within the B8 use approved by outline 22/01829/OUT, and explains why officers treated data centres as B8 rather than sui generis. The applicant's cover letter describes eight data-centre buildings with data halls, and its September 2026 statement for 26/02446/REM confirms that 25/03310/REM, for 8 data-centre buildings, was approved on 6 August 2026. The consent therefore covers the data-centre buildings themselves, not only enabling or utility works.

locator.precision: Area centroid of the 32.3 ha application-site polygon that Cherwell District Council's public planning register map service holds for 25/03310/REM (and, identically, for outline 22/01829/OUT), computed in British National Grid (459269.85, 219831.94) and converted to WGS84 with pyproj 3.7.1. It falls inside the boundary, 190 m from the nearest edge, within the main cleared site; it is not a building footprint or surveyed position.
locator.identity_review: The map-service feature carries the same application reference (25/03310/REM), location ('Unit D1 Graven Hill, Circular Road, Ambrosden'), status (Permitted) and decision date (6 August 2026) as the decision notice, and its 323,339 m2 area matches the 32.3 ha site in the officer report. The applicant's application form gives a site point of easting 459219, northing 219802, 59 m from the centroid and inside the same polygon. In Esri World Imagery viewed locally (not redistributed), the polygon encloses the cleared former MOD depot between the railway and a solar farm, south of St David's Barracks, with its access-road corridor running north-east to the A41 roundabout, as the officer report describes; the centroid lies in the cleared main site. No geocoder, town centre or estate centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The council publishes no positional accuracy for the application boundary, and the centroid represents a 32.3 ha site whose eight units extend several hundred metres around it.
